successors.note: 'The site of the Mycenaean Pylos then seems to have been abandoned during the Dark Ages (1100-800 BC).' The land passed to no state (eu-01-a's convention for the palace destructions).

capitals.name: Pylos (Palace of Nestor, Ano Englianos)
capitals.note: 'close to the road 4 kilometres south of Chora and 17 kilometres north of Pylos'; the palace as 'the administrative, political, and financial centre of Mycenaean Messenia'; coordinates approximate. The palace dates only from artifacts 'dating from 1300 BC'.

correction.text: the Mycenaean state of Pylos, 'covered an area of 2,000 km2' (a 25 km disc round Pylos, 1,963 km2)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Mycenaean Greece (-1500..-1101) draws the Peloponnese as one shape and has no Pylos. The page gives the area: 'The Mycenaean state of Pylos (1600-1200 BC) covered an area of 2,000 km2' with 'a minimum population of 50,000 according to the Linear B tablets'. A 25 km disc round Pylos is 1,963 km2 (ratio 0.98); the modern Messenia regional unit is 2,991 km2 (Messenia page), so the Pylian state was roughly two thirds of it. The page gives no boundary ('the Pylia Province' is the wider area).

region.text: the Mycenaean state of Pylos, 'covered an area of 2,000 km2' (a 25 km disc round Pylos, 1,963 km2)

ledger.note: c. 1600: the Mycenaean state of Pylos. 'The Mycenaean state of Pylos (1600-1200 BC) covered an area of 2,000 km2' and 'became the capital of one of the most important human centers of this civilization and of a powerful kingdom'. The page gives no rise date apart from the range; the Palace of Nestor page dates the finds 'from 1300 BC'. The 25 km disc is the researcher's reading of the 2,000 km2.

region.text: the Mycenaean state of Pylos, 'covered an area of 2,000 km2' (a 25 km disc round Pylos, 1,963 km2)

ledger.note: c. 1180: fire destroys the palace of Pylos. 'It was destroyed by fire around 1180 BC'; the Linear B tablets 'mention hasty defence preparations due to an imminent attack without giving any detail about the attacking force'. The page also ends the state at 1200 and the Palace of Nestor page dates the fire 'around 1250 BC'.

certainty.note: No boundary is known; the area (2,000 km2) is the page's, the shape is a disc.

sources.title: Pylos
sources.note: State 1600-1200, area 2,000 km2, population 50,000, destroyed by fire around 1180, abandoned in the Dark Ages.

sources.title: Messenia
sources.note: Only the modern regional unit area, 2,991 km2 (cited in the keyframe note as a sanity check).

sources.title: Palace of Nestor
sources.note: Palace site, finds from 1300 BC, fire 'around 1250 BC', ~1,000 Linear B tablets; silent on provinces and extent.

notes: A palace state inside Cliopatria's Mycenaean Greece (-1500..-1101, written as mycenaean-greece by eu-01-a): the renderer should carve this disc out of that shape. The two pages disagree on the end: 1200 (state range, Pylos page), 1180 (Pylos page, fire), 1250 (Palace of Nestor page); the dossier ends at 1180 (as eu-01-a's palace caption does). The Pylos page is silent on the Hither and Further Provinces and the districts of the Linear B state, and on any frontier with the neighbouring palaces. Gazetteer names used that it lacks: Pylos (place). Related: mycenaean-greece, greek-dark-ages, kingdom-of-mycenae, minoan-civilization.
